158320.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
158320.text: A party of women out in a sleigh fills this wood engraving, which Winslow Homer drew for the magazine Harper's Weekly; it was published on January 2, 1869. A man with a moustache and spectacles holds the reins at the front. Beside him sits a woman in a fur-trimmed coat, and four more women crowd in behind, one in a feathered hat turning to look back over her shoulder. A thick fur blanket hangs over the back of the sleigh, and the seat backs are decorated with a monogram. Sleigh bells hang from the horse's harness. Behind them, two men drive a second sleigh, and further back a child looks out from another sleigh while someone waves a white cloth. Bare winter trees line the snowy ground.

54305.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
54305.text:
A boy stands on a shaggy rug just inside an open front door, wrapped against the cold in a cap, a long knitted scarf pulled up over his mouth, a brown coat and heavy boots with snow on them. A large bundle of holly is tied to his back with a rope, and beside him on the floor is a basket of fruit. From the right, a hand reaches into the picture, holding out a plate with a slice of cake and a small glass of dark red drink. Through the doorway lies a snowy garden with iron railings and small birds in flight.

George Baxter made this print in 1859. It combines a steel engraving printed in black with colours printed from blocks, and the surface is varnished.

19333.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
19333.text:
Food is set out on a plain wooden table against a dark background. A woven basket heaped with chestnuts stands at the centre. To the right, two round, flat cakes or loaves are stacked on a crumpled sheet of white paper. In the foreground lie three pale mushrooms, two of them turned over to show their gills, a small bunch of black grapes, and a grey plate of shelled nuts. The painter has picked out the weave of the basket and the shine on the chestnuts and grapes.

The museum attributes this oil painting to the Italian artist Paolo Antonio Barbieri and dates it to about 1640.

149018.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
149018.text:
This Nativity is painted on vellum inside a large initial letter H, framed by leafy blue, green and red ornament and gold leaf. Mary kneels on the left in a blue cloak dotted with gold, her hands together in prayer. The Christ Child lies on the ground before her, surrounded by golden rays, and Joseph stands on the right in a yellow cloak. Behind them, under a wooden shelter with a straw roof, an ox and a donkey look out over a manger filled with hay. A gold star sends a ray down towards the child, and two groups of angels with gold haloes pray at the upper right. Beyond the shelter rise green hills with fields, buildings and a castle on a peak.

It was made by Zanino di Pietro in the Veneto region of Italy, between 1430 and 1440.

105660.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
105660.text: Snow falls on a broad street lined with brick houses in this hand-coloured aquatint, engraved by George Hunt after a painting by James Pollard. Horse-drawn coaches crowd the road. The largest carries passengers in top hats on its roof, along with luggage and a bundle of evergreen branches with red berries, and dead birds and other game hang from its sides. The coach is lettered with the names Sudbury, Norwich and Bury. Snow lies on the roofs and frosts the trees, and shop signs advertise rum, brandy and wines. In the lower right corner, a group of boys rolls a giant snowball while another bends to make a snowball of his own. At the lower left, a woman stands with a boy and a small dog.

43678.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
43678.text:
A fair-haired girl in a long pink-red dress leans against a large black bear lying on the grass, holding a sprig of white flowers up in one hand. A second girl, dressed in white with flowers in her hair, lies on her back beside the bear. On the right, under the trees, a figure in a red hooded cloak sits next to a spinning wheel. Behind them rise blue mountains, dark fir trees and trees in autumn colours. The title names the fairy tale of Snow White and Rose Red.

Richard Doyle made this small picture in watercolour over pencil on ivory paper.

26601.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
26601.text:
Snow falls against a deep blue sky in this street scene. On the left, a tall signboard painted with large black characters stands on a wooden trestle. In the middle, a figure in a wide straw hat walks towards a wooden bridge, carrying a load of pink boxes. Beyond the bridge, a stone wall is topped with snow-covered pine trees, and a tower rises in the distance. On the right, baskets hang under the snowy roof of a shop, beside a cart wheel, and two dogs stand in the snow.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige comes from his series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo and is dated 1858.

77673.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
77673.text:
A small girl with black hair tied up on top of her head walks across a green floor, carrying a bowl that holds a miniature pine tree and a branch of pink plum blossom. She wears a dark kimono patterned in green and white. Behind her, grey sliding screens are decorated with white bamboo. On the floor to the left, a teapot sits on a small brazier.

The panel below the picture explains the title: "Pine: long life, family love, needles radiating from a common centre. Plum: grace and sweetness. Bamboo: purity, integrity, straight, white within. All for friendship that no winter storms can harm." Helen Hyde made this colour woodcut on Japanese paper in 1913.

130552.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
130552.text:
Towering rocks covered in snow fill this mountain view, with snow still falling from a grey sky. A red wooden bridge arches over a deep gorge, where a blue stream runs between the rocks. Two small figures approach the bridge from the left. Above it, a red building with a snow-covered roof stands on top of a rock, and to the right a long building with an open veranda looks out over the gorge. Tall conifers covered in snow crowd the slopes behind.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, dated 1853, comes from his series Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces.

25743.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
25743.text:
This round painting sets the Adoration of the Magi in front of a ruined classical building, with plants growing from its cracked stonework. Mary sits on the steps holding the Christ Child, and Joseph stands on a step beside them, leaning on a staff. One king kneels before them in a pink robe, with gifts on the ground nearby, while others in rich robes stand close by. Their followers crowd the scene with horses and a camel. A peacock perches on the roof on the right, an ox lies near the building, sheep stand in the foreground, and a small monkey sits on a stone block. In the distance on the left, a ship lies at anchor below rocky hills.

The museum attributes this tempera painting on panel to Raffaello Botticini and dates it to about 1495.

109220.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
109220.text:
An angel appears out of dark clouds at the top of this painting, above a group of shepherds and their animals. In the foreground, a man in a broad hat sits playing a pipe. Behind him, a young man leans over a sheep, and a woman kneels with her back to us beside a large brown cow. On the right, another man rests his head on his arm next to an ox. Goats and more sheep crowd around them, and a thick tree trunk rises on the left.

This oil painting was made around 1710, after a composition by Jacopo Bassano.

65940.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
65940.text:
A tabletop is crowded with fruit and pottery against a dark red background. On the left, a white fluted bowl is heaped with pears and other fruit. Behind it stand two jugs, a tall pink one with a curved handle and a darker red one, and to the right is a cream-coloured bowl with a small spout. More pears and round green fruit lie loose on the red-brown tablecloth. The shapes are painted with thick, visible brushstrokes and outlined in dark paint.

Marsden Hartley painted this oil on canvas in 1923.

28875.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
28875.text:
A full moon shines over a thatched cottage half hidden by trees. Light streams from its open doorway onto the path. In the foreground, a man in a hat drives a small flock of sheep along the lane, while a smaller figure stands nearby with a dog and another figure leans on the garden gate. A tall fir tree rises on the right against the night sky. The whole scene is built up from fine, dense lines that leave only the moon, the doorway and a few highlights bright.

Samuel Palmer made this etching, titled Christmas, around 1850. It is signed "S. Palmer" in the lower right corner.

59656.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
59656.text:
Frost covers the trees and bushes around an old water mill with a thatched roof and a large wooden wheel. Water spills through a wooden sluice gate under a narrow footbridge into a frozen pond. In the foreground, a little girl in a blue dress stands on the ice next to a small child sitting in the snow, and a girl in red stands among the frosted reeds on the right. A man in a top hat looks down from the mill wall. Tall bare trees rise against a pale sky, and the word "Winter" is engraved below the picture.

George Baxter made this print in 1849. It combines etching, aquatint and stipple printed in purple with colours printed from blocks.

25428.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
25428.text:
Tall pine trees heavy with snow stand in the grounds of a shrine on a clear winter day. On the left are red shrine buildings with snow-covered roofs. Small figures with umbrellas walk across the snowy courtyard, past stone lanterns and a gateway. In the middle, a white-blossomed tree is covered in snow, and on the right the view opens out over the snowy rooftops of the city below.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, made around 1840 to 1842, comes from his series Famous Places in the Eastern Capital.

156299.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
156299.text:
Three long stockings hang from the edge of a mantelpiece in this quick pencil sketch. A candlestick and a few other objects stand on the mantelpiece. The dark opening of the fireplace below is shaded in with heavy strokes.

William Michael Harnett drew this in graphite on tan paper. It is not dated.

81640.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
81640.text:
A line of travellers wrapped in cloaks and hoods makes its way across a wide, snowy shore, leaving footprints behind them. Some carry bundles or bags, some lean on walking sticks, and one carries a load of branches on his back. On the right, pine trees and red-tinged shrubs grow on a rocky slope. Across the water, a village sits on the far shore, and pale mountains line the horizon.

Kitao Masayoshi (also known as Kuwagata Keisai) made this colour woodblock print in the 1790s.

22442.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
22442.text:
Five boys work together to roll an enormous snowball across the snow. One boy on the right and another bending low in front pull on a rope wrapped round the ball. A third boy holds a long bamboo pole, a fourth looks up over the top of the ball, and a fifth, at the back, holds his hands to his mouth as if to warm them. Above them hang branches weighed down with snow, and a tree trunk leans in from the left. The boys wear patterned clothes in soft greens and oranges, and the boy on the right wears wooden sandals.

The museum attributes this colour woodblock print to Isoda Koryusai and dates it to about 1772.

20965.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
20965.text:
Two young women and a girl gather round a large dog made of snow. The girl reaches up to the snow dog's face, and a young woman bends over it, resting a hand on its head. Both wear brown kimonos patterned with orange maple leaves. On the right, a woman in a white robe stands watching, her hands wrapped in an orange cloth. Behind them are snow-covered pine branches and bushes, a red post rises at the top right, and the sky is printed in warm yellow.

Suzuki Harunobu made this colour woodblock print around 1767 to 1768. It is signed on the right.

158368.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
158368.text:
This double page from Harper's Weekly is framed with garlands of holly. The words "A Merry Christmas and Happy New Year" arch across the top. In the centre, a round picture shows the Nativity, with Mary holding the Christ Child while an old man kneels before them and others look on. In the upper corners are two winter street scenes with horse-drawn sleighs, one labelled 5th Avenue. The lower half shows a Christmas party: children dance in a ring while adults watch, and a decorated Christmas tree stands on the right.

Winslow Homer made this wood engraving, which was published on December 24, 1859.

71532.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
71532.text:
The Nativity fills a large initial letter P, drawn in green and pink with blue leaves against a gold background. Joseph stands on the left with a walking stick, in a blue hat and red cloak, and Mary kneels beside him in a blue mantle with her hands together. On the right, under a shelter with a green roof, the Christ Child lies wrapped in the manger, which has woven green sides. An ox and a donkey lean over him, two angels look down from behind the roof, and sheep graze below. Trees and buildings appear in the background, and a small star shines at the top.

This cutting from a choir book is painted in tempera and gold leaf on parchment. The museum gives it to the Master of the Brussels Initials and dates it to about 1390.

54287.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
54287.text:
Mary kneels with her hands together beside a woven manger, where the Christ Child lies on a white cloth over straw. Joseph, an old man with a white beard, stands on the left leaning on a staff. Shepherds crowd in from the right: one holds a crook, an old man and a young man lean close, and a man with a red cloth over his shoulder kneels with a small child. A lamb lies on the ground in front of the manger. Two winged infants fly overhead holding a ribbon, and the wooden stable stands on the right under a cloudy sky.

George Baxter made this print in 1852, combining etching, aquatint and stipple with colours printed from 14 blocks.

23842.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
23842.text:
Snow falls on a street lined with fences and houses. On the left, one person carries another on their back, and the passenger holds a large paper umbrella over them both. In the middle, a man walks along with a black box hanging from a pole on his shoulder. Behind him, a figure in a straw cloak and wide hat bends low, with pine branches on his back, as two puppies play in the snow. A New Year decoration of straw, pine and a round orange fruit hangs over the gateway. A woman looks out from a balcony on the right, sparrows perch on the roof, and a plum tree blossoms above the fence.

This colour woodblock print by Kitagawa Utamaro is a double-page illustration from the poetry anthology The Young God Ebisu, published for the New Year of 1789.

25614.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
25614.text:
This print is made of three sheets placed side by side. On the left, a woman in a blue kimono decorated with large flowers stands beside a snow-covered tree and a small fence. On the right, a figure in red and orange robes walks through the snow holding a large white umbrella, next to a lantern on a post and a snowy gateway. The middle sheet opens onto a winter landscape: a village of snow-covered roofs, an arched bridge over a river, a white hill, and birds flying beneath snowy pine branches.

The colour woodblock print, from the series Fashionable Genji, was designed by Utagawa Kunisada I and Utagawa Hiroshige around 1853.

114835.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
114835.text:
Mary sits on a stone step holding the Christ Child, who reaches towards an old king with a white beard kneeling before them in a golden robe. The kneeling king offers a golden vessel. Behind him, a second king in a red robe holds up a gold cup, and a third, in a green cloak with a sword at his side, steps forward from the right. Joseph stands on the left. Ruined arches rise behind the group, and pale mountains appear in the distance. A handwritten inscription runs along the lower edge.

This watercolour over pencil was made in 1827 after a painting by Bonifazio de' Pitati, called Bonifazio Veronese.

111041.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
111041.text:
Steam rises from a large copper pot on the left of this kitchen table. In front of it lie leeks and carrots, and in the centre a raw leg of mutton rests on a white cloth. To the right, a shallow copper dish holds eggs with their yolks showing, and behind it sits a dark green cabbage. A small dark container stands in the foreground, and white and orange-red cloths hang down on the right. The paint is applied loosely, with soft, visible brushstrokes.

This oil painting by an unknown French artist dates from between 1780 and 1790.

47742.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
47742.text:
This print is shaped like a round fan. Snow falls on a street of shops at night. On the right, two women walk through the snow under red umbrellas, holding up the hems of their patterned kimonos. On the left, a large stone lantern capped with snow stands behind a white fence, next to a stone animal statue and a snow-laden tree. Further along the street, small figures hurry past under umbrellas. A red label at the top left gives the title, "Snow".

Utagawa Hiroshige made this colour woodblock print, from the series Famous Places of Edo, around 1849 to 1852. It is signed "Hiroshige ga".

22842.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
22842.text:
Five children play together beneath a straw rope hung with paper streamers. A child in a black hat dances on the left, beating a small hand drum. Another child in a tall black hat and patterned robes holds an open fan. In the foreground, three children kneel on the floor: one holds the string of a kite lying on the ground, and another, in a pink kimono with a flower pattern, looks up at the dancers. On the right stands a box holding a small pine tree and other decorations.

Torii Kiyonaga made this colour woodblock print, from the series Precious Children's Games of the Five Festivals, around 1801. It is signed "Kiyonaga ga".

222528.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
222528.text:
Couples whirl round a crowded room in this etching titled "December: Christmas Bustle". A sign above the far wall reads "Saloon of Fashion", and posters advertise goods such as "Bears Grease", "Macassar Oil" and "Otto of Roses". On the left, a fiddler plays for the dancers. In the centre, two lit candles stand on a stand against the back wall. Onlookers crowd the edges of the room, and on the right a man sits at a table with food.

This steel etching by George Cruikshank comes from George Cruikshank's Steel Etchings to The Comic Almanacks. It is dated 1840 and was printed around 1880.

8913.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
8913.text:
Two figures walk close together through the snow under a single umbrella with a thick layer of snow on top. One wears a black robe with a black hood; the other, in white with a white hood, holds the umbrella. Both wear tall wooden sandals. Branches heavy with snow hang down from the top of the picture, and a dark tree trunk rises on the right. Apart from a few patterned edges and sashes, the print uses only black, white and soft browns.

Suzuki Harunobu made this colour woodblock print around 1767. His signature is on the right.

9893.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
9893.text:
Snow falls on temple grounds beside a blue pond. A pagoda rises above trees thick with snow, and red temple buildings with white roofs stand on the left. Small figures under umbrellas and wide hats walk along the path by the water. On the right, a small hall stands on top of a snowy hill among the trees.

Utagawa Kuniyoshi made this colour woodblock print in 1853. It is signed "Kuniyoshi ga" and carries the seal of the publisher Maruya Seijiro.

25436.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
25436.text:
Snow falls on the grounds of a shrine built around a pond. In the foreground, a steep arched bridge curves over the water, and stone lanterns capped with snow stand on the bank. A long trellis stretches across the pond on the left. On the right are red shrine buildings with snow-covered roofs, and a figure under a wide umbrella crosses a second arched bridge towards them. Snowy pines and other trees fill the background.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, made around 1832 to 1838, comes from his series Famous Places in the Eastern Capital.

89976.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
89976.text:
Snow falls on a temple complex beside a river. A five-storey pagoda rises on the right, and large red temple halls with snow-laden roofs stand behind snow-covered trees. A small stone bridge crosses the water, and figures in wide hats walk along the snowy banks. In the foreground, the river curves in bright blue past a stone wall.

Utagawa Hiroshige made this colour woodblock print in the tenth month of 1852. It is signed "Hiroshige ga".

25023.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
25023.text:
This tall, narrow print looks down on a temple in heavy snow. On the lower left is a red gateway with large hanging lanterns, and a five-storey pagoda rises on the right above trees covered in snow. Below, a crowd of small figures under umbrellas and wide hats makes its way along a snowy path. Large flakes fill the grey sky.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige is dated 1840 and comes from his series Famous Views of the Eastern Capital.

89001.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
89001.text:
Two children roll a large snowball in front of a red wooden building whose roof is covered with snow and overhung with snowy branches. On the left, a child leans over the snowball with his hand to his mouth. On the right, a child in a yellow and blue checked kimono pushes it, while a young woman in a pink kimono stands behind with a hand on the child's shoulder. All three wear tall wooden sandals in the snow.

Suzuki Harunobu made this colour woodblock print around 1767. It is signed "Harunobu ga".

29544.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
29544.text:
Mount Fuji rises white against a blue sky in the upper left, with a second mountain below it, and a band of yellow light glows along the horizon on the right. In the foreground, two travellers cross the snow towards an arched wooden bridge. One wears a straw raincoat and a wide hat and carries a load on a pole; the other, in a brown coat, walks ahead. Tall pines heavy with snow stand beside a winding river, a second bridge crosses it further back, and thatched houses sit under thick snow on either side.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, dated 1855, is number 13 in his series Famous Sights of the Fifty-three Stations, also known as the Vertical Tokaido.

60651.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
60651.text:
Three women make their way through falling snow across three joined sheets. On the left, a woman stands in front of a red building and snowy shrubs, holding a closed umbrella with a black-and-white pattern. In the middle, a woman bends into the wind under an open umbrella, her patterned kimono blowing around her. On the right, a woman with a scarf over her head carries a tray with a large bowl. Snowy hills and trees stretch across the background.

Utagawa Kunisada I made this colour woodblock triptych around 1844. Its title presents the scene as a parody of Liu Bei visiting Zhuge Liang in wind and snow.

10932.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
10932.text:
Snow falls on a canal lined with steep white banks. Small boats covered in snow are moored on the water, and an arched bridge crosses it further along. On the right, a long building with white walls and a red gateway faces the street, where figures walk under umbrellas and wide hats past small snow-covered trees. A tall tower stands among snowy pines on the hill at the top right, and a pagoda rises in the distance on the left.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, made around 1843 to 1847, comes from his series Famous Places in the Eastern Capital.

77318.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
77318.text:
A tall shrine gateway printed in blue stands in the snow, with a plaque at its centre and snow along its crossbeams. Stone lanterns capped with snow line a blue fence on either side. Women in colourful kimonos walk through the gateway holding umbrellas against the falling snow, leaving footprints behind them. Snow-laden pines and other trees stand on both sides, with snowy roofs behind the fence.

This colour woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige, made around 1834, comes from his series Famous Places in Kyoto.

21687.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
21687.text:
A large household of women is busy cleaning a house. On the left, a woman kneels to sweep with a red brush, and a tall woven blind leans against the wall. In the middle, a group of women stands close together. On the right, a woman carries a tray of cups, another kneels by a wooden bucket, and a folding screen painted with bamboo leans against stacked floor mats. Large paper lanterns with a leaf crest hang from the ceiling.

This colour woodblock print by Kitagawa Utamaro, made in the late 1790s, is made up of the three left sheets of a set of five.

59615.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
59615.text:
A full moon lights a mountain scene at night. Climbers with long poles pick their way across deep cracks in a field of snow and ice in the foreground. Behind them, a line of small figures climbs a long snowy slope towards a group gathered near the top. Jagged rocky peaks rise against the dark sky.

This print by George Baxter, from Ascent of Mont Blanc, is dated 1855. It combines etching, aquatint and stipple printed in blue with colours printed from blocks.

24418.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
24418.text:
Four women in patterned kimonos stand on a terrace of a temple. Three stand close together on the left, and a fourth, on the right, points at a large black lacquered structure covered with a pink cloth. Behind them rises a tall pine tree, and long covered walkways lead off into the temple grounds, where small figures walk across an open courtyard. A large black barrel bound with rope stands on the right.

Utagawa Toyohiro made this colour woodblock print around 1804 to 1810. It is the centre right sheet of a set of five, and it is signed "Toyohiro ga".

21174.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
21174.text:
A heap of puppies huddles together in the snow. Some are white, some spotted with black, and one is orange; a few sleep curled up while others look out. Behind them grow white daffodils with long green leaves. Above, snow lies along the edge of a thatched roof, snowflakes fall against a green sky, and soft yellow clouds frame the top of the picture.

Isoda Koryusai made this colour woodblock print around 1773. It is signed on the left.

7578.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
7578.text:
Five children build a huge snowman. One stands behind the large lower ball and lifts a smaller ball high overhead. A child on the left covers their face with both hands, another leans in from the right, and two more run up from the front. The children wear loose clothes in pinks and greens, and lines of flowing calligraphy run down from the top of the sheet. The soft colours are printed without black outlines.

Kitao Shigemasa made this colour woodblock print in a narrow upright format around 1764. It is signed at the lower right.

87073.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
87073.text:
Two sparrows fly and perch among the branches of a camellia in falling snow. One swoops down from above with its wings spread, and the other sits on a branch below, looking up with its beak open. Snow lies thickly on the dark green leaves and on the bright red camellia flowers. The sky darkens to black at the top of this tall, narrow print.

Utagawa Hiroshige made this colour woodblock print around 1837 to 1848. It is signed "Hiroshige fude".

151899.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
151899.text:
This tall, narrow strip of decoration once formed part of the border of a choir book page. At the top, curling blue and red leaves twist round each other. Below them grows a stem of flowers: a red carnation, a white daisy, a purple four-petalled flower, a blue star-shaped flower and others, with two ripe red strawberries. A small bird with a pinkish crest and a long beak perches in the middle. The background is scattered with tiny gold and black dots, and a gold band frames the edge.

This manuscript cutting is painted in tempera, coloured inks and gold leaf on vellum. The museum records it as European and does not give a date.

16629.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
16629.text:
A blue-and-white dish is heaped with fruit and vegetables: lemons, pomegranates, purple aubergines and green leaves. More lie on the white cloth in front of it, including a large aubergine, red and orange peppers, tomatoes and a pomegranate. The background is painted in soft, blurred greens and blues, and short, lively brushstrokes catch the light on each surface.

Pierre-Auguste Renoir painted this oil on canvas in 1881. It is inscribed "Renoir 81" in the lower left corner.

27952.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
27952.text:
A thick slice of orange melon stands upright on the left. On the right is a green glazed jar with a handle over the top and a small spout. In front of them, two fish lie side by side on a sheet of yellow paper on the table. The paint is laid on thickly in short, dense strokes, with dark outlines round each object. The name "Vincent" is painted in the lower left corner.

This oil painting on panel is dated around 1888. The museum describes its painter as an imitator of Vincent van Gogh.

16410.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
16410.text:
A woman in a white cap and apron leans over a wooden barrel in a dim, barn-like room with heavy wooden beams. Around her the floor is crowded with household things: wooden tubs, earthenware jugs and pots, a large wicker basket, a metal plate and a blue-and-white china plate. Bones and an animal skull lie on the floor, and a cat sleeps in the lower right corner. A rooster stands on the left, and a hen perches on top of the basket on the right.

Hendrik Martensz. Sorgh painted this oil on panel in 1657.

185775.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
185775.text:
A peacock with a long, colourful tail stands on a path in the foreground of this view across the terrace of a villa. Tall umbrella pines rise beside a stone wall topped with a large urn. A woman in red and white walks on the left, and two figures sit near the wall. On the right, a stone balustrade leads the eye past the terrace to distant hills and the valley below. Warm, cloudy light fills the sky.

Richard Parkes Bonington painted this view in oil on millboard in 1826.

16417.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
16417.text:
A young man in a feathered cap sits on a wooden chair playing a small pipe. Beside him, an old woman in a white cap leans across a table, holding a sheet of paper and watching him. On the table stand a brown stoneware jug with a metal lid and a small glass. In the doorway behind, a man in a hat looks in. The room is dark, with light falling on the faces and the young man's sleeves.

David Teniers the Younger painted this oil on panel between 1635 and 1640.

81568.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
81568.text:
The towers and spire of Notre-Dame cathedral rise across the river in Paris. On the riverside walk in the foreground, two nuns in black habits and white headdresses walk side by side. Nearby, a man sits beneath a tree with a small dog, and another pushes a handcart. Trees with brown autumn leaves line the embankment, a street lamp stands among them, and carriages cross the bridge in the distance. Fallen leaves cover the wet ground.

Jean François Raffaëlli painted this oil on composition board around 1890. It is signed in the lower left corner.

104106.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
104106.text:
Two young women walk across a small park, each carrying a wicker basket full of white laundry on her hip. One wears a blue patterned blouse, the other a white blouse and cap, and both wear long dark skirts. Behind them, a figure dressed in black walks past with a small dog, and a street of tall buildings and carriages stretches into the distance. The trees have only a few yellow leaves left, and the light is pale.

Jean François Raffaëlli painted this oil on panel around 1890. It is signed in the lower right corner.

111667.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
111667.text:
A crowd in eighteenth-century dress gathers for a festival in this loosely painted sketch. Men in red coats and black cloaks and women in wide silk dresses stand about in groups, talking and pointing. On the left, a garland of greenery hangs from a wooden post and beam. Further back, a man runs across the open square after a dog, and another dog runs past behind the beam. A small white dog lies on the ground at the foot of the post, and a gilded shield stands in the middle of the crowd.

Giovanni Paolo Panini painted this oil on canvas in 1729.

186425.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
186425.text:
An elderly man and woman sit side by side at a small round table set for tea. He has a white beard and wears a fur cap and a brown coat; she wears a white bonnet tied with a ribbon and a dark dress. On the table are a white teapot, a cream jug, a bowl, two cups on saucers and a pink-and-white cloth. Behind them, a striped cat sits on a window sill between pots of flowers, one with bright red blooms.

Jean François Raffaëlli painted this oil on canvas around 1880. It is signed in the lower right corner.

94241.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
94241.text:
A woman in a grey and dark red dress sits in a red armchair with her eyes lowered, in a room with deep red walls and a red sofa. At her feet, a small child in a pink dress plays on a patterned rug strewn with scraps of white paper. On the left is a fireplace surrounded by blue-and-white tiles, with a clock and a vase of flowers on the mantelpiece. On the right, a single lit candle in a brass candlestick stands on a dark round table.

Félix Vallotton painted this oil on board in 1899. It is signed in the lower right corner.

160229.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
160229.text:
A long path runs between low stone walls under a row of tall white pillars, in bright sunlight. Orange trees heavy with fruit grow on both sides, and a few oranges have fallen onto the path. On the wall on the left stands a large terracotta pot holding a pink rose bush. Halfway down the path, a man in a hat walks along holding a sheet of paper, and a gate closes the far end. Shadows of leaves fall across the pillars.

Thomas Fearnley painted this oil on paper, later mounted on canvas, around 1834. It is signed in the lower right corner.

160032.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
160032.text:
Two women decorate a room with roses in this tall, narrow painting. One stands on a ladder against a white column, wearing a pale robe, an olive-green drape and a gold band in her hair, and she reaches down for a garland of roses and leaves. Below her, a second woman in white kneels and lifts the garland up to her, holding a long yellow ribbon. Behind them are red walls and carved columns. A basket full of roses sits at the lower left, more roses lie scattered across the mosaic floor, and a dark glass vase stands on the right.

Edward John Poynter painted this oil on canvas in 1875. It carries his monogram and the date in the lower left corner.

81555.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
81555.text:
Three people sit over the remains of lunch under a green trellis arbour beside a river. On the left, a bearded man in a light jacket faces a woman in a dark dress, who sits with her back to us. On the right, a man in a white shirt leans back in his chair with one hand raised. The tablecloth holds bottles, wine glasses and a plate with a bunch of grapes. Beyond the trellis, red flowers bloom and rowing boats glide across the bright, shimmering water.

Pierre-Auguste Renoir painted this oil on canvas in 1875. It is inscribed "Renoir" in the lower left corner.

80475.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
80475.text:
A waterfall tumbles over dark rocks, half buried in snow and ice, into a swirling green pool. Snow covers the banks on both sides. Above the falls stand a long pink building and a smaller house, and another small pink building sits on the rocks at the lower left. Behind them, dark conifers climb the slopes of a snowy mountain under a pale sky. The paint is laid on in thick, broken strokes of white, blue and violet.

Ernest Lawson painted this oil on canvas in 1919. It is signed and dated in the lower right corner.

81521.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
81521.text:
A young man in a pale shirt raises a heavy axe high above his head, about to bring it down. Beside him is a large pile of split wood, with a hat and a blue cloth lying on top and another axe leaning against it. On the right, a saw rests on a wooden sawhorse, and thick logs lie on the ground. Behind him, a dark wall of forest fills most of the picture, with a strip of grey sky at the top.

Jean-François Millet painted this oil on canvas around 1858 to 1866. It is stamped "J.F. Millet" in the lower right corner.

117700.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
117700.text:
A nude woman in a cap sits on a patterned cloth on a riverbank, seen from behind, with her knees drawn up and her hands raised to her head. Beside her, an open parasol with a striped border lies on the ground, and a straw hat trimmed with flowers rests on the cloth. Sunlight flickers through the leaves onto her back and sparkles on the water beyond. The whole picture is built up from small dabs of pale blue, green and yellow.

Frederick Carl Frieseke painted this oil on canvas around 1915. It is signed in blue paint on the grass in the lower right corner.

21165.by: Claude Opus 5.5, from the image and the AIC catalogue record
21165.text:
Two women sit outdoors talking. On the left is a woman in a cream dress trimmed with black lace. On the right, a woman in a white dress and a bonnet tied with a dark ribbon sits on a green folding stool. Two parasols, one dark and one white with a fringe, shade them. Trees and a cloudy sky fill the background, and the paint is applied in quick, loose strokes.

Marcellin Gilbert Desboutin painted this oil on canvas between 1875 and 1879. It is signed in the lower right corner.
